items.title: Searching "Boots" lists all three boots with count 3
covers: Expected step 1: every product whose name contains Boots, count matching
items.reason: This is the reported bug: a word at the end of a name ("Boots") returned `count: 0` because the filter only matched name prefixes. Functional layer against real Postgres is the cheapest layer that runs the actual SQL translation of the filter; a unit test with in-memory LINQ would not catch a wrong SQL operator.

items.title: Searching "Hiking Boots" lists Wanderer Black Hiking Boots
covers: Expected step 2: Hiking Boots lists Wanderer Black Hiking Boots
items.reason: Step 2 of the bug: a multi-word phrase (with an encoded space) from the middle/end of a name returned nothing. It is a separate case from TC-BUG-49-01 because it checks that the whole phrase is matched as one substring, including the space, not word by word. Functional layer for the real SQL translation.

items.title: Searching the name prefix "Wanderer" still lists Wanderer Black Hiking Boots
covers: Expected step 3: Wanderer still lists Wanderer Black Hiking Boots, as today
items.reason: Regression guard: the fix must not break the search that already worked (text at the start of the name). Separate from TC-BUG-49-01/02 because a contains-only bug (for example matching only after a space) would fail here but pass there. Functional layer for the real SQL translation.

items.title: Searching lowercase "boots" stays case-sensitive and finds nothing
covers: Expected: the letter case of the search text behaves exactly as today
items.reason: The story requires case handling to stay exactly as today (case-sensitive; case-insensitive search is tracked separately). A fix using `ToLower`/`ILIKE` would make "boots" return the three boots, silently changing behaviour; this case catches that. Today "boots" returns no items, and with contains-matching it must still return none because no name contains lowercase "boots". Functional layer because case sensitivity depends on the SQL the database runs.
